subject: AR1 correlation parameter in a space-time model

messages.author: 958272119e13f0e7
messages.subject: AR1 correlation parameter in a space-time model
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to implement a space-time model in INLA, using an matern spde for the spatial element and an AR1 process for the time-steps. I have followed the example of Cameletti  et al 2012 on the website and found it to be very useful. However, I can't figure out how to get the marginal distribution of the AR1 correlation parameter out of my model fit. Cameletti et al suggest:

>result$summary.hyperpar["GroupRho for field",]

and can get marginals from
>results$marginals.hyperpar.

However, in version of INLA I'm running, the closest I get is:
> res$summary.hyperpar
                      mean        sd 0.025quant  0.5quant 0.975quant      mode
Theta1 for field  4.115378 0.6337380   2.909351  4.100337   5.396918  4.056174
Theta2 for field -5.734316 0.6030074  -6.952359 -5.719592  -4.582772 -5.676797
>

Neither of which are the Rho that I'm looking for - and the marginals.hyperpar has disappeared.

So this looks to me like INLA has changed in the four years since Cameletti et al and that functionality is no-longer there. What does one do today?

Best wishes,

Mark

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] AR1 correlation parameter in a space-time model
parts:
Hi Mark,

I see that you have two objects: 'result' and 'res'. Additionally, you
have to use ["GroupRho"] instead.

Elias

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] AR1 correlation parameter in a space-time model
parts:
On 08/03/16 12:01, Mark R Payne wrote:
> >result$summary.hyperpar["GroupRho for field",]

This works if the name of the index is 'field'. The short 'GroupRho'
$summary.hyperpar["GroupRho",]
wil also works as long there is only one 'group' model.

Elias

Hi,

when I run the Cameletti2012 case study code I get

> result$summary.hyperpar
mean sd 0.025quant
Precision for the Gaussian observations 30.7498496 1.294954874 28.2667976
Theta1 for field 3.1987460 0.058799065 3.0812255
Theta2 for field -4.5823646 0.061402715 -4.7050934
GroupRho for field 0.9596968 0.006654978 0.9457317
0.5quant 0.975quant mode
Precision for the Gaussian observations 30.7292537 33.3580790 30.694953
Theta1 for field 3.1996017 3.3119755 3.202157
Theta2 for field -4.5814690 -4.4641221 -4.578795
GroupRho for field 0.9599804 0.9717876 0.960331

just as expected. That indicates that the problem is in your code and
we'll need more details to figure out why you don't get "GroupRho for
field" in your output.

Alternatively, there is an issue with the specific R/INLA combination
you have. Your INLA installation is a bit old, so upgrading might be a
first step, but be aware that newer versions might not work on older R
versions so be sure to backup your installation before upgrading!

Finn

messages.author: 958272119e13f0e7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] AR1 correlation parameter in a space-time model
parts:
Ah-ha! I found it. I there are two different objects in play here:

>mdl <- inla(....)

>field.res <- inla.spde.result(inla=mdl,....)

mdl contains marginals for the hyperparameter, but field.res does not.
Both objects contain summaries for the hyperparameter, but the contents
are different:

> rownames(mdl$summary.hyperpar)
[1] "Precision for the Gaussian observations"
[2] "Theta1 for field"
[3] "Theta2 for field"
[4] "GroupRho for field"
> rownames(field.res$summary.hyperpar)
[1] "Theta1 for field" "Theta2 for field"
>

I was looking in field.res, but should have been looking in mdl instead.

Thanks for the help.

Mark
